chunks: And Yūnus ibn Yaʿqūb narrated from his brother Yūsuf:

Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام asked for water, and a cup made of brass containing water was brought to him. Then one of those sitting with him said to him, “Indeed, ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī dislikes drinking from brass.” He said, “Then ask him: is it gold or silver?”

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, referred to by his kunyah
key_terms.ذَهَبٌ: gold, one of the metals prohibited for such use
key_terms.فِضَّةٌ: silver, one of the metals prohibited for such use

ai.seo_question: Is drinking from brass vessels disliked or prohibited in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith relates that Imam Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام was brought water in a brass vessel, and when someone mentioned that ʿAbbād al-Baṣrī disliked drinking from brass, the Imam replied by distinguishing brass from gold and silver. The report indicates a jurisprudential focus on the specific prohibition of gold and silver utensils rather than extending dislike or prohibition to brass without proof.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.4240 - Yunus bin Yaqub narrated from his brother Yusuf:

Abu Abdullah (as), once asked for water, and a vessel made of brass containing water was brought to him.
One of those sitting with him said: "'Abbad al-Basri dislikes drinking from brass vessels."
Imam (as) said: "Then ask him, is it gold or silver?"
